Testing an Indirect Effect with MBCO

Source: vignettes/articles/mbco.Rmd
mbco.Rmd

mbco() tests a restriction on a fitted model with a likelihood-ratio test. This page shows the whole path for one indirect effect: what is tested, which route to use, a worked example, how to read the result, and what to do with the warnings. It links to the Cookbook and the Technical Notes for the details instead of repeating them.

What MBCO tests

MBCO stands for model-based constrained optimization. You fit two nested models to the same data:

  • h1, the full model, with every path free;
  • h0, the restricted model, with the restriction you want to test (for an indirect effect, one path or the product a*b fixed at 0).

mbco(h0, h1) returns the likelihood-ratio statistic and its p-value. A small p-value is evidence against the restriction.

An indirect effect a*b is zero when a = 0 or b = 0. That is a union of two nulls, so a valid test rejects only if every single-path null is rejected (an intersection-union test). mbco_product_null() does exactly that; one nonlinear constraint a*b == 0 does not, and can land on the wrong branch (see below).

Pick a route

You have Use type Reference distribution
OpenMx fits mbco(h0, h1) "asymp" chi-squared
OpenMx fits mbco(h0, h1, type = "semi") "semi" semiparametric bootstrap, R replicates
OpenMx fits mbco(h0, h1, type = "parametric") "parametric" parametric bootstrap, R replicates
Two medfit SEMFit fits mbco(h0, h1) "asymp" only chi-squared, no OpenMx, no refit
A product null with OpenMx mbco_product_null(full, paths = c("a", "b")) any OpenMx type one single-path null per path; the result of the largest p-value

The bootstrap types cost R fit pairs; "asymp" costs one. The SEMFit route needs medfit 0.8.0 or later, supports no bootstrap and no OpenMx fitting controls, and is shown in Cookbook recipe 10.

A worked example

The data are memory_exp: an experiment on instructions to use imagery or repetition, with recall as the outcome. The full model has two mediators, with paths a1, a2 (from x) and b1, b2 (to recall).

d <- as.data.frame(memory_exp) # mxData() rejects tibbles
d$x <- as.numeric(d$x) - 1
manifests <- c("x", "repetition", "imagery", "recall")
model <- OpenMx::mxModel(
  "full", type = "RAM", manifestVars = manifests,
  OpenMx::mxPath("x", c("repetition", "imagery", "recall"), arrows = 1,
                 free = TRUE, values = 0.2, labels = c("a1", "a2", "cp")),
  OpenMx::mxPath("repetition", "recall", arrows = 1, free = TRUE, values = 0.2, labels = "b1"),
  OpenMx::mxPath("imagery", "recall", arrows = 1, free = TRUE, values = 0.2, labels = "b2"),
  OpenMx::mxPath(manifests, arrows = 2, free = TRUE, values = 0.8),
  OpenMx::mxPath("one", manifests, arrows = 1, free = TRUE, values = 0.1),
  OpenMx::mxData(d, type = "raw")
)
invisible(utils::capture.output(
  full <- suppressMessages(OpenMx::mxTryHard(model, checkHess = FALSE, silent = TRUE))
))

Test the product a1*b1 = 0 

res <- mbco_product_null(full, paths = c("a1", "b1"), type = "asymp")
res
#> MBCO Test Result
#> ================
#> Test type: asymp 
#> Chi-squared statistic: 0.0831 
#> Degrees of freedom: 1 
#> P-value: 0.7731 
#> Significance: ns (not significant)
#> Note: product null; binding single-path null: b1 = 0.
#> Provenance:
#>   Packages: RMediation 1.11.0, OpenMx 2.22.11, medfit 0.3.2, R 4.6.2 
#>   Test: type = asymp
#>   RNG: Mersenne-Twister / Inversion / Rejection 
#>   Run at: 2026-11-09 22:45:26 UTC 
#>   Seed: not recorded (call set.seed() yourself and report it)

The note under the result names the binding branch: the single-path null (a1 = 0 or b1 = 0) with the largest p-value. That branch is the test of the indirect effect.

Test one path

For a single path, build h0 from the unfitted model and fit it yourself:

null_b1 <- OpenMx::mxModel(model, name = "b1_eq0", OpenMx::mxConstraint(b1 == 0, name = "c"))
invisible(utils::capture.output(
  h0 <- suppressMessages(OpenMx::mxTryHard(null_b1, checkHess = FALSE, silent = TRUE))
))
mbco(h0, full, type = "asymp")
#> MBCO Test Result
#> ================
#> Test type: asymp 
#> Chi-squared statistic: 0.0831 
#> Degrees of freedom: 1 
#> P-value: 0.7731 
#> Significance: ns (not significant)
#> Provenance:
#>   Packages: RMediation 1.11.0, OpenMx 2.22.11, medfit 0.3.2, R 4.6.2 
#>   Test: type = asymp
#>   RNG: Mersenne-Twister / Inversion / Rejection 
#>   Run at: 2026-11-09 22:45:27 UTC 
#>   Seed: not recorded (call set.seed() yourself and report it)

Building h0 from the unfitted model matters: a fitted h0 keeps no starting values, which is the information mbco() needs to tell a dropped constraint from an accepted violation (next section).

Read the result

An mbco() result is an MBCOResult. Use the slots, or $ and [[:

Slot Holds
@statistic, @df, @p_value the likelihood-ratio statistic, its degrees of freedom and p-value
@type "asymp", "semi" or "parametric"
@refit NULL, or the tighter tolerance and the statistic before and after, when h0 had to be refit
@branch the single-path null that gave the result, from mbco_product_null(); otherwise NULL
@dropped bootstrap replicates that did not converge and were left out; NULL without a bootstrap
@provenance what produced the result: package and R versions, type, R, RNGkind(), run time 
res@p_value
#> [1] 0.7731401
res@branch
#> [1] "b1"
res@dropped    # NULL: no bootstrap here
#> NULL
names(res@provenance)
#> [1] "rmediation" "openmx"     "medfit"     "r"          "type"      
#> [6] "R"          "rng_kind"   "time"

The bootstrap p-value is mean(null > observed) over the kept replicates: strict >, no +1 (see Technical Notes, section 3). The seed is not recorded in @provenance, because it cannot be recovered afterward: call set.seed() before a bootstrap and report the seed with the result.

Warnings and errors that matter

Class Kind What to do
RMediation_constraint_violation warning A constraint of h0 is violated at the fitted solution. mbco() refits at a tighter tolerance and uses that statistic; read @refit.
RMediation_constraint_not_enforced warning h0 fit equals h1 fit although a constraint was violated. OpenMx may have silently dropped the constraint (OpenMx#433); for a product null, use mbco_product_null().
RMediation_h0_refit_failed error The refit could not repair h0. No statistic is returned from a fit known to be invalid.
RMediation_bootstrap_too_many_dropped error More than 5% of replicates did not converge. Check the model, or raise R.
RMediation_bootstrap_infeasible error A replicate’s constraint violation could not be repaired.

The full explanation, with the reasons, is in Technical Notes, sections 2 and 3, and the same table is on the Quick Reference.
